thread:
maya.support: Heads up — customer ACME reports our quota heatmap shows a big zero block (12:00–12:30 UTC) but their requests were getting 429s. They sent example request IDs.
alex-sre: Can you paste one of the request ids and the customer org id? I want to cross-check enforcer logs.
maya.support: org=acme-prod req=rc_1a2b3c4d — they attached a screenshot of the console heatmap showing no activity for that window.
sam-support: I pulled enforcer logs for that org — tons of throttles around 12:07. Looks like counts are in enforcer but not in the dashboard aggregate.
jordan-eng: Possible culprits: ingestion sampler, aggregator windowing mismatch, or Kafka consumer lag. Any alerts around that time?
sre-bot: ALERT: kafka-consumer-lag service/usage-aggregator spiked to 18k msgs at 12:06 UTC, consumer group usage-agg-consumer lag > 300s for ~6m
alex-sre: kafka lag would explain missing rows in the aggregator. If the aggregator fell behind it might drop or re-window messages. Need to verify what the aggregator does on rebalance.
maya.support: Repro steps customer gave:
- send 200 req/s for org acme-prod between 12:00–12:10
- many 429s started at 12:05
they said console still shows empty heatmap for 12:00–12:30
jordan-eng: Quick check for missing data:
```
SELECT window_start, sum(count) FROM usage_aggregates
WHERE org_id='acme-prod' AND window_start >= '2025-12-01T11:55:00Z'
GROUP BY window_start ORDER BY window_start;
```
If aggregator writes partial windows with a different window_start alignment, we'd see zeros.
sam-support: Ran that query — 12:00 window has 0 rows, 12:05 shows values but small. Enforcer logs show ~14k throttled tokens between 12:04 and 12:08.
jordan-eng: Hmm. Two hypotheses:
1) Aggregator sampling config was set to 0.01 for that consumer (downsampling) due to a hot path rollback earlier today.
2) Aggregator uses a rolling 5m window that only emits on complete ticks; if consumer lag caused emission to skip, the dashboard's heatmap code (which queries fixed 5m buckets) will show zero.
alex-sre: Can you check aggregator config for that deployment? `env AGG_SAMPLE_RATE` and `AGG_WINDOW=rolling` maybe.
ops-lead: I just checked infra - there was a Canary rollback at 11:58 that toggled SAMPLE_RATE to 0.01 for usage-topic in cluster eu-west-1. It should have been staged only for the canary tenant but was flipped for all.
maya.support: That would explain why enforcer still counted throttles (it records at the gateway), but the aggregator only forwarded 1% of messages so dashboard missed the pattern.
sam-support: Action items:
- ops: revert SAMPLE_RATE for usage-aggregator to 1.0 in eu-west-1 (done 12:40 UTC)
- eng: reprocess missing windows from raw topic for acme-prod (replay from offset 0 for 12:00–12:10)
- support: notify customer and explain root cause and fix ETA
jordan-eng: For reprocess we'll run the replay job with this command:
```
./bin/replay-usage --topic=usage-raw --org=acme-prod --start=2025-12-01T12:00:00Z --end=2025-12-01T12:10:00Z --write-mode=aggregate
```
I'll kick it off and watch write throughput.
alex-sre: Also adding a test in CI to ensure SAMPLE_RATE changes are gated per-tenant and not global.
ops-lead: Reprocessed windows with replay job — new aggregates landed at 12:52 UTC. Heatmap now shows expected activity for 12:00–12:10.
maya.support: Customer updated — heatmap now matches enforcer counts. They want a post-mortem and assurance this won't recur.
jordan-eng: I'll open a short postmortem and include: (1) root cause: mis-scoped canary toggle of SAMPLE_RATE, (2) mitigation: per-tenant gating + alert on sample_rate changes, (3) remediation: replay + data backfill complete, (4) follow-up: CI check and runbook update.
sam-support: Marking this resolved for now. Customer notified and closure scheduled.
alex-sre: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
notes: Root cause: accidental global flip of aggregator sampling rate during canary rollback; enforcer (source-of-truth) continued recording throttles. Fix: revert config and replay raw topic to backfill dashboard aggregates. Follow-ups: per-tenant config gating + CI guard + alerting on sample-rate drift.
